subject: Model identification: How to standardize the variance of a latent variable

messages.author: 0964d4061cf3f269
messages.subject: Model identification: How to standardize the variance of a latent variable
parts:
Hi everyone,

there are typically two ways to set the metric of the latent variables: (1) for each latent variable, fix the factor loading of one of the indicators (typically the first) to a constant (conventionally 1.0), or
(2) standardize the variances of the latent variables.

I noticed that the sem function of lavaan does automatically fix the factor loading of the first indicator to 1. Does anybody know the command to standardize the variance of the latent variable to 1?

Greetings, Philipp

messages.author: 671b14edc9322fa7
messages.subject: Re: Model identification: How to standardize the variance of a latent variable
parts:
Hi

Model identification by fixing the latent variable variances to one requires complex linear constrains on model parameters because the variances of endogenous latent variables are not model parameters, but something that depends on the variances of exogenous latent variables, path estimates, and estimated unique variances. It is not a common practice to do this but it is fairly common that fixing the unique variances of latent variables to one is confused with fixing the latent variable variances.

Check the std.lv and auto.fix.first options.

When I want to have results where all latent variables are standardized, I typically identify the model with the first indicator rule and then standardize after estimation. Intepreting a model that has been identified by fixing the unique variances can be difficult because it is not intuitively clear what the scale of the endogenous latent variables would be.

Mikko
